clue.text: Great king imprisoning a fair lady within fort

indicators.note: a fort that imprisons something holds it inside its walls
within places the preceding words inside the word that follows

parts.note: a pah (or pa) is a Maori fortified village
taken as written
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A mighty monarch locks a beautiful woman away inside his stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: Padishah is a Persian title, used of the Shah or the Ottoman sultan, meaning a supreme or great ruler.

clue.text: When appearing in press that's cast aside, they hardly pause to look

something cast is thrown about, or moulded into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
by means aside, as in 'stand by' or 'put by'

explanation.surface: Something discarded after being in the newspapers barely gets a second glance from anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: PASSE (out of date) tempts as the 'cast aside' piece, but 'cast' rearranges PRESS and 'aside' is BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Passers-by are people walking past, who by definition do not stop to watch.

clue.text: Marine fish to exhaust with a rod at sea

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Catching a sea fish wears you out when you fish with a rod offshore.
explanation.definitionFit: The dorado is a large ocean game fish, also called mahi-mahi or dolphinfish.

clue.text: Unruly Goth studded with metal, performing illegal stunts

clue.text: A&M volume that's all right removed from pulpit

clue.text: Male entranced by goddess revealing bust

clue.text: After gallons strong drink makes you morose

clue.text: Indian village producing chana

clue.text: So yes, this does for the answer — irregular masonry does

indicators.note: Azed's formula says these words plus the solution are a rearrangement of the phrase that follows

parts.note: letters taken away from the longer phrase
the full set of letters that are shared out

explanation.surface: A sly instruction that seems to admit its own trick, then praises rough stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive anagram: SO YES plus the answer together rearrange MASONRY DOES, so remove S, O, Y, E, S from that phrase and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Random masonry, or random rubble, is stonework laid with stones of irregular sizes and no regular courses.

clue.text: Whom subtenant maybe pays to speak about crooked lender?

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whom a subletting tenant pays rent to, then complaining about a dishonest moneylender.

clue.text: Forward breaks a leg, completely losing it once near

parts.note: quite means completely, as in 'quite right'

explanation.surface: A rugby forward fractures a leg and totally loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Pin is slang for a leg, and a prop is a front-row rugby forward. 'Once' marks the definition as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Appropinque is an old word, from Latin appropinquare, meaning to approach or draw near.

clue.text: Kylie Minogue's No. 1 follows hostile reception, then terrible anger

taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kylie Minogue' reads as one name, but Kylie alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kylie is a Western Australian Aboriginal word for a boomerang, the curved throwing stick.

parts.note: last letter of the word

clue.text: Bingo making bishop lustful

clue.text: Old slaver that is off isle with hand on board

explanation.definitionFit: Spawl is an archaic word for spittle, which is what slaver (drool) means.

clue.text: Quick peek that shows Jock's great when given lift in cast

clue.text: Votive deity card distributed, filled with love

love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

clue.text: Song for audience, 'A wee strip o' plaid'?

clue.text: Bagpiper's drone maybe causing irritated mumble

clue.text: Unruly kid let off in quarrel

clue.text: Lots of ashes farmers put in two thirds of slurry mixed

clue.text: Child clutching end of train leapt once
